enquiry: We produce an opaque, concentrated milk product that flows through a processing line. We currently sample it for fat and protein analysis and would like earlier information about composition changes. Product temperature and texture vary during production. We want an initial spectroscopy concept and a practical comparison experiment, while retaining our laboratory checks.

clarification_questions.question: What goes wrong today when fat or protein composition changes are detected only from lab samples, and what decision would real-time data drive?
clarification_questions.why: Defines the process decision and the value of earlier information.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Decision and delay impact unknown; the first step is to clarify the pain before choosing a method.

clarification_questions.question: What are the target fat and protein levels, their expected variation range, and are they expressed as ppm or as %?
clarification_questions.why: Determines required sensitivity and whether lab screening must cover trace or major-component levels.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Level unknown; lab screening establishes whether fat and protein are ppm or % level and their spread.

clarification_questions.question: At the measuring point, is the product a liquid, paste or soft solid, and how does its opacity vary?
clarification_questions.why: Sample form and optical properties decide the probe geometry (diffuse reflection, transflection or ATR).
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Opaque concentrated product assumed; physical form at the measuring point unknown and to be confirmed in lab screening.

clarification_questions.question: How do temperature, texture, and fouling vary along the line, and what cleaning or sterilization regime applies to the measuring point?
clarification_questions.why: Temperature and texture change the spectra and affect probe contact, fouling and calibration robustness.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Temperature and texture vary as stated; their range and cleaning regime are unknown and must be measured in the in-line trial.

clarification_questions.question: Where on the line could the probe be installed, what is the distance to the analyzer, and are any existing fibers or optical access points available?
clarification_questions.why: Distance and available fibers determine feasible wavelength range and whether remote measurement is possible.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Installation point and distance unknown; a provisional lab setup is assumed until the line layout is known.

clarification_questions.question: Which laboratory method is used for fat and protein today, what is its accuracy and repeatability, and how often are samples taken?
clarification_questions.why: The reference method defines what the spectroscopic comparison must be checked against.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Reference method and accuracy unknown; the expert obtains the existing lab procedure before the comparison design.

clarification_questions.question: What accuracy and response time would make earlier information useful, and what budget applies?
clarification_questions.why: Sets the performance target and whether a simple few-wavelength sensor or a broader lab system is justified.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Requirements unknown; the comparison design starts with lab screening to establish achievable performance.

recommendations.geometry: Diffuse reflection probe, flush-mounted in the line

reason.text: The dairy example supports inline NIR reflection for opaque or highly concentrated products such as whole milk concentrates.

caveat.text: Reflection is sensitive to surface characteristics and fat globule size, so these factors should be checked on this product.

recommendations.confidence_reason: The application example matches the sample type, but nothing has been measured and product ranges are unknown.

reason.text: The dairy example notes that a transflection probe may suit both low-fat and high-fat milk products.

caveat.text: Transmission fails when milk is too thick or fat-rich, so transflection must be tested against reflection on this product.

recommendations.confidence_reason: The example covers milk products, not this opaque concentrate; suitability is a hypothesis to test.

items.text: Diffuse reflection probe at the flowing product as primary candidate; transflection probe as comparison if a light path is feasible.

Vis-NIR silica fibers transmit about 350-2400 nm, so the upper end of the 780-2500 nm NIR range may not be covered; link length is undefined.

risks.text: A change in formulation or matrix can invalidate a fat or protein calibration.

assumptions: Product is treated as a flowing liquid or paste until the measuring point is confirmed.
Transmission alone is not assumed suitable for this opaque product.

steps.text: Collect samples across the agreed fat and protein range and the temperature and texture variation of production.
Record reflection and transflection spectra from each candidate, with independent laboratory reference measurements and timing information.
Build single-method models first; validate on held-out production runs before any combination is considered.
Compare prediction error, bias and ability to follow changes against the client's accuracy and response-time requirements.

feasibility_plan.afs_next_path_reason: Depends on lab screening results and the measuring-point layout.

decision_basis.text: Agree accuracy, bias and response-time criteria with the client before testing; choose the simplest configuration meeting them on independent production runs.

flags_before_revision.detail: not_supported: The cited page S01 p.17 says reflection is sensitive to surface characteristics and fat globule size. It does not mention temperature or texture effects, so the claim that 'temperature and texture effects must be tested' goes beyond the page. Fix: Limit the caveat to what the page says: reflection is sensitive to surface characteristics and fat globule size, so these factors should be checked on this product.

not_supported: The cited page S01 p.7 mentions sample inhomogeneity, process turbulence, and scattering overlap, but nowhere mentions temperature or texture changes mimicking composition changes. Fix: Rephrase to what the page supports, e.g. 'Morphological factors such as inhomogeneity or process turbulence must be considered, since scattering overlaps with other phenomena.'

RAMAN.nominal_range: Raman shift in cm-1; signal recorded in the visible / short-wave NIR (400-1100 nm); state the laser excitation separately [S01 p.11]

FLUO.nominal_range: UV/Vis excitation and emission; depends on the fluorescent species [S01 p.12]

UVVIS.nominal_range: UV 190-360 nm and visible; depends on target and setup [S01 p.5]

rule_hints: nominal_range_not_instrument_range: A nominal method range is not the usable range of a specific instrument, fiber or probe. [DOCX §3; DOCX §5]
do_not_invent: Do not invent measured results, accuracy, detection limits, response times, fiber lengths, product codes or prices, client facts, or guarantees. [DOCX §3]
insufficient_information_is_valid: If the known facts cannot justify a method choice, say so, ask the deciding questions and propose the next step. [DOCX §3]
